questions.question: If the simple interest on a certain sum of money for 15 months at 9.6% per annum exceeds the simple interest on the same sum for 8 months at 11.4% by Rs. 1,320, then the sum is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The simple interest on a certain sum of money for 15 months at 9.6% per annum exceeds the simple interest on the same sum for 8 months at 11.4% by Rs. 1,320

**Concept used:**

S.I = (P × T × R)/100

Here, P = Sum, T = Time & R = Rate 

**Calculation:**

Let the sum be P

Now, [P × 15/12 × 9.6/100] - [P × 8/12 × 11.4/100] = 1320

⇒ 0.12P - 0.076P = 1320

⇒ 0.044P = 1320

⇒ P = 1320/0.044

⇒ P = 30000

**∴ The sum is Rs. 30,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Calculation:**

According to the question,

Principal is constant. So

⇒ (15/12) × 9.6% - (8/12) × 11.4% = 1320

⇒ (12 - 7.6)% = 1320

⇒ 4.4% = 1320

⇒ 100 % = (1320/4.4) × 100 = Rs. 30,000

**∴ The correct answer is 30,000.**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 39,000 is divided among A, B, C such that A's share is (1)/(3) of B and B gets 20% more than C. A's share is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum = Rs. 39000

**Calculation:**

Let the share of C be 5x

So, share of B = 5x + 5x × 20% = 6x

Share of A = 6x × (1)/(3) = 2x

Ratio of share = 2x : 6x : 5x

⇒ 2 : 6 : 5

Amount A got = 39000 × (2/13) = 6000

**∴ A's share is Rs. 6,000.**

questions.question: A retailer buys a tracksuit for Rs. 850. His overhead expenses are Rs. 50. If he sells the tracksuit for Rs. 1,170, then what is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:

A retailer buys a tracksuit for Rs. 850.

His overhead expenses are Rs. 50.

**Concept used:**

Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Profit% = (Profit/Cost price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Total cost of a tracksuit = 850 + 50 = 900

Profit on selling a tracksuit at 1170 

⇒ 1170 - 900 = 270

Profit% = (270/900) × 100 = 30%

**∴ His profit percentage is 30%.**

questions.question: A sum of money becomes double in 5 years at compound interest rate. The same sum of money will be 4 times of itself in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal(P) doubles itself in 5 years when compounded annually

**Formula used:**

Amount(A) = P[1 + (R/100)]T

Here, P = Sum, R = Rate of interest & T = time period

**Calculation: **

According to the question: 2P = P[1 + (R/100)]⁵

⇒ 2 = [1 + (R/100)]⁵

⇒ (2)¹/⁵ = 1 + (R/100) ----(i)

Let the required time period be T years

⇒ 4P = P[1 + (R/100)]T ----(ii)

From (i) and (ii), we get

4 = [(2)¹/⁵]T

⇒ 4⁵ = 2T

⇒ (2²)⁵ = 2T

⇒ 210 = 2T

⇒ T = 10

**∴ It will become 4 times in 10 years.**

questions.question: In a toy factory, a worker can assemble a toy in 5 minutes. If, from 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., 1248 toys are to be assembled, then how many workers should be employed?
questions.solution:

A worker can assemble a toy in 5 minutes

Time duration is from 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.

1248 toys are to be assembled

**Calculation:**

From 10:30 am to 12:30 pm total time = 2 hours or 120 min [As 1 hours = 60 min]

Let the number of workers required to be x

x workers can assemble x number of toys in 5 minutes

So, x workers can assemble 24x number of toys in 120 minutes

According to the question,

24x = 1248

⇒ x = 52

**∴ 52 workers should be employed.**

questions.question: 6 men and 8 women can complete as much work in a given time as 3 men and 13 women. If a man can complete a work in 12 days, then in how many days will 4 women be able to complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

6 men and 8 women can complete as much work in a given time as 3 men and 13 women

A man can complete a work in 12 days

**Concept used:**

Total work = efficiency of the workers × time taken by them

**Calculation:**

6 men + 8 women = 3 men + 13 women

⇒ 3 men = 5 women

⇒ men/women = 5/3

So, the efficiency of men and women is 5 units and 3 units

Now, Total work = 12 × 5 = 60 units

4 women be able to complete the same work in

Required time = 60/(4 × 3) = 5

**∴ Required answer is 5 days.**

questions.question: The circumference of a circle of diameter 14 cm is the same as the perimeter of a square. The area of the square is (take π = (22)/(7)):
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The circumference of a circle of diameter 14 cm is the same as the perimeter of a square.

Circumference of a circle = 2πr

Area of a square = a²

The perimeter of a square = 4a

Here, r = radius of the circle & a = side of the square

**Calculation:**

The radius of the circle = 14/2 = 7 cm

Let the side of the square be 'a'

Now, 2 × (22/7) × 7 = 4 × a

⇒ 44 = 4a

⇒ a = 11

Now, Area of the square = 11² = 121

**∴ The area of the square is 121 cm2**.

questions.question: The price of a commodity has increased by 20%. The Gupta family reframed their monthly budget and plans to spend 8% more money on that particular commodity. By what percentage should they reduce its consumption so as to manage with the increased amount of money?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The price of a commodity has increased by 20%. 

The Gupta family reframed their monthly budget and plans to spend 8% more money on that particular commodity.

**Calculation:**

Let the intial price of the commodity be 10x

New price of the commodity 

⇒ 10x × 120% = 12x

Let previously they spend 100y in a month on that commodity

Now they planned to spend 100y × 108% = 108y

No. of commodity they get on the previous price

⇒ 100y/10x = (10y/x)

Now they will get 108y/12x = (9y/x)

Reduction in consumtion = (10y/x) - (9y/x) = y/x

% of reduction = (frac{y)/(x)}{(10y)/(x)}×100

⇒ (y)/(10y)×100 = 10

**∴ They should reduce its consumption by 10% so as to manage with the increased amount of money.**

questions.question: The LCM of two numbers is 45 times their HCF, and the sum of the LCM and HCF is 1518. If one of the numbers is divided by 16, the quotient is 18 and the remainder is 9. What is the other number?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The LCM of two numbers is 45 times their HCF, and the sum of the LCM and HCF is 1518.

**Calculation:**

Let the HCF of the numbers be x

So, LCM is 45x

Now, 45x + x = 1518

⇒ 46x = 1518

⇒ x = 33

So, HCF is 33

LCM = 33 × 45

As we know HCF is also a factor of those two numbers

Now,

We need to divide 45 into two such ways that both co-prime each other

45 = 9 × 5 and 9 and 5 are co-prime 

So, the two numbers are 33 × 9 = 297 and 33 × 5 = 165

Now, in the option, we only have 165

**∴ The required number is 165.**

questions.question: If the ratio of the base radii of a cylinder and a cone is 1 ∶ 2 and that of their heights is 2 ∶ 1, then what is the ratio of the volume of the cylinder to that of the cone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of radii of base = 1 : 2

Ratio of heights = 2 : 1

**Formula used:**

Volume of cone = 1/3 πr²h

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

**Calculation:**

Let the radius of the cylinder and a cone are x and 2x, respectively.

The height of the cylinder and cone are 2y and y, respectively.

According to the question,

The volume of the cylinder = π × x² × 2y

⇒ 2πx²y 

The volume of the cone = (1/3) × π × 4x² × y

⇒ (4πx²y)/3

Required Ratio = 2πx2y : (4πx2y)/3

⇒ 3 ∶ 2 

**∴ The ratio of the volume of the cylinder to that of the cone is 3 : 2.**

Two students A and B appeared in a class test. B scored 40% of the sum total of their marks, which is 7 less than the marks of A. How many marks did B score?
questions.solution:

B scored 40% of the sum total of their marks, which is 7 less than the marks of A.

**Calculation:**

Marks of A = Marks of B + 7

According to the question,

B = (A + B) × 40/100

⇒ B = 2A/5 + 2B/5

⇒ B – 2B/5 = 2A/5

⇒ (5B - 2B)/5 = 2A/5

⇒ 3B/5 = 2A/5

⇒ A/B = 3/2 = 3 : 2

Difference of marks = (3 - 2) = 1 unit = 7 marks

⇒ The marks of B (2 units) = 2 × 7 = 14 marks

**∴ B scored 14.**

questions.question: If 62% of a number is equal to three-fifth of another number, then what is the ratio of the first number to the second number?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

62% of a number is equal to three-fifth of another number

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

(62/100) × 1st number = (3/5) × 2nd number

⇒ (62/20) × 1st number = 3 × 2nd number

⇒ 62 × 1st number = 60 × 2nd number

⇒ 1st number/2nd number = 60/62

⇒ 1st number/2nd number = 30/31

So, ratio = 30 : 31

**∴ The first number to the second number is 30 : 31.**

Average speed = 2ab/(a + b)

Here,

a = speed at time of going

b = speed at time of coming back

S = (2 × 48 × 32)/(48 + 32)
